page_title: Uptick — Free, Open-Source App Updater for Mac

sources.entry: Uptick - Open-source app updater that finds updates from the App Store, Sparkle, Electron feeds and Homebrew, and verifies each download before installing. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/chengffei/uptick)

summary.name: Uptick
summary.one_liner: Uptick is a free, open-source macOS app updater that finds updates for installed apps from their own update channels and installs them after checking each download.
keywords: update mac apps in one click
use_cases: Find which installed Mac apps have newer versions
Update Sparkle-based Mac apps in one click
Update Electron apps from their own feeds
Replace MacUpdater for keeping apps current
Verify an app update before installing it from Terminal
Keep Homebrew-cask-listed apps updated without running Homebrew
summary.what_it_does: Uptick reads the version of each app in the Applications folder and queries the app's update channel: Mac App Store lookup, Sparkle appcast, Electron update feed, or Homebrew's public cask list. It lists outdated apps and, when you press Update, downloads the new version and checks that the bundle ID, developer team ID and signature match the installed app before swapping it in. The old copy goes to the Trash, and it restores the old one if copying fails. It also has a CLI for listing, verifying and installing updates. App Store apps are handled by opening the App Store page because macOS no longer lets other apps install those updates.
notable: Verifies bundle ID, team ID and signature of each download before installing
Uses four update sources with no Uptick server or telemetry
Includes a command-line interface using the same engine
Successor to MacUpdater, which stopped development in January 2026
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so first launch needs approval in System Settings or use of the one-line installer
App Store apps open the App Store to update rather than being updated directly
